ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence under Article 14 Ley 10/2010 and Articles 21-25 Real Decreto 304/2014 covering politically exposed persons (PEPs), coupled with mandatory screening against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (including Council Regulation (EC) 2580/2001 and Regulation (EU) 833/2014 as amended regarding Russia/Ukraine), and the United States OFAC SDN List as a market-standard control for USD-denominated SWIFT and SBLC payment rails. Positive hits trigger immediate filing of a Suspicious Transaction Report (Reporte de Transacción Sospechosa) with SEPBLAC, provisional freezing of the contemplated transaction, and refusal to proceed absent express regulatory clearance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) - negative name certification (certificación negativa de denominación social) obtained through the electronic office of the Colegio de Registradores de España (www.registradores.org) or through the CIRCE single-window platform (www.circe.es); paper filing remains available at Calle Príncipe de Vergara 94, 28006 Madrid.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate denomination must be lawful, truthful, and not misleading; it must be written in Latin characters and ordinarily in Spanish or another official language of the European Union, with foreign names romanized and phonetically adapted to Spanish orthography. The entity type must be expressed as 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada', 'S.L.' or 'S.R.L.'. Abbreviations, punctuations and symbols are not permitted, and the name may not be identical or typographically/phonetically similar to any registered denomination (Articles 405-413 Reglamento del Registro Mercantil).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The negative name certificate lapses if incorporation is not completed within ninety days of issue; no statutory extension is available, and a fresh application must be submitted. If the Registro Mercantil Central rejects a proposed denomination on grounds of identity, phonetic similarity, or misleading content, the applicant may first file an optional administrative appeal (recurso potestativo de reposición) before the same authority within one month of notification, and thereafter a direct administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) within one month before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública of the Ministerio de la Presidencia, Justicia y Relaciones con las Cortes, in accordance with Articles 114-123 Ley 39/2015, de 1 de octubre, of the Common Administrative Procedure. The appeal should attach comparative registry printouts, trademark titles, or authorization documents for sensitive tokens. While the appeal is pending, the applicant may simultaneously reserve alternative names; if the appeal succeeds, the originally requested name is certified with the same ninety-day validity.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual or co-working addresses are tolerated by the Mercantile Registry only where an identifiable administrative base exists in Spain, namely personnel present during office hours, reception of notifications, and actual location of management. For an ISIC 4661 wholesale marine-fuel brokerage holding a statutory hydrocarbons license and classified as High_Risk_Special_License from an AML standpoint, a mere virtual mailbox or serviced P.O. box does not meet the substance expectations of SEPBLAC, AEAT for excise on hydrocarbons, the energy regulator, and bank counterparties. A physical office with personnel, records and governance apparatus is required in practice under Articles 9 and 346 Ley de Sociedades de Capital.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 75% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first twelve months of registration, given the regulated wholesale-petroleum-products status under Ley 34/1998, AEAT supervision of the Impuesto sobre Hidrocarburos, and SEPBLAC's risk-based inspection cycle applicable to High_Risk_Special_License entities.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, Texto Refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Articles 4.2, 20-22, 58-59, 62, 210-212); Ley 14/2013, de 27 de septiembre, de apoyo a los emprendedores y su internacionalización (expedited SL formation, Articles 30-33); Reglamento del Registro Mercantil (Real Decreto 1784/1996).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (name certification), Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office (enrollment and legal personality), and the Ventanilla Única Empresarial/CIRCE single-window portal for electronic incorporation filings.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (notarized deed of incorporation) filed with the provincial Registro Mercantil, preceded by a Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social and documented payment of notarial and registry aranceles.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Article 4.2 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital imposes a minimum fully subscribed and paid-up capital of EUR 3,000 for an Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada; notwithstanding the metadata flag 'minimum_capital_requirement': false, the statutory floor is mandatory. The capital must be deposited in a Spanish bank incorporation account (cuenta de constitución), evidenced by a certificado de depósito or notarial capital statement, and remains blocked until the deed is registered at the commercial registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company approves the subscription and full payment of the share capital of EUR 3,000, allocated as set forth in the deed of incorporation, and hereby ratifies the allotment of participations to each founding member. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company shall be established at [address], Madrid, within the territorial scope of the Commercial Registry. FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed sole director (Administrador Único), with all statutory powers, for an indefinite term, accepting the office. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the director is authorized to execute the public deed, obtain the provisional tax identification number, open corporate bank accounts, and file all registrations required under the Ley de Sociedades de Capital.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign party identification and NIE acquisition
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Consulate in the residence jurisdiction or the Oficina de Extranjería (Comisaría General de Extranjería y Fronteras) for in-country processing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Each non-resident founding member and the intended sole director must obtain a Número de Identificación de Extranjero (NIE) before notarial execution. File form EX-15, passport, criminal record certificate and proof of payment of fee 790-012, or apply through the Consulate for an initial visa/NIE. Non-resident corporate shareholders must obtain a non-resident NIF via form 036 through a tax representative.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or national identity document
Form EX-15 or consular visa application
Certificate of criminal record from the country of residence (apostilled)
Proof of payment of Tasa 790-012
If corporate shareholder: certificate of incorporation, director register, and fiscal representative appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected, correct formal defects and re-file; alternatively, appoint a person holding an NIE as incorporation attorney-in-fact (representante) to execute the deed, then regularize the NIE after incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name clearance (Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) via the CIRCE/RMC online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a digital application for a negative name certificate listing one or more proposed corporate names. The RMC verifies that the proposed name does not coincide with or is not confusingly similar to existing Spanish companies. The certificate is issued electronically and is valid for three months, renewable once for an additional three months.
required_dossiers: Application for negative name certificate
Proposed corporate names in Spanish
NIE or passport of the applicant
Payment of the RMC fee (approximately EUR 14)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is reserved or rejected, file the second and third alternative names from the list; request a renewal or extension before the certificate expires.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of incorporation escrow account and deposit of share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution (Santander, BBVA, CaixaBank or equivalent) — corporate banking department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate account named 'S.L. en constitución' and deposit the minimum capital of EUR 3,000. The bank issues a certificado de depósito identifying the depositors and an unavailability clause blocking disposal until the deed is presented to the commercial registry. Alternatively, in-kind contributions are supported by a directors' valuation report.
required_dossiers: Passport or NIE of each founding member
Name certificate issued by the RMC
Draft bylaws (estatutos)
AML/beneficial ownership declaration (declaración de titular real)
KYC forms and source-of-funds evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines the account, apply to another institution or execute the deed after the notary records the notarial capital statement, with a two-month term to open the deposit; for enhanced due diligence in the petroleum sector, provide commercial contracts and the license pipeline to satisfy the KYC file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the public deed of incorporation before a notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary of the Iltre. Colegio Notarial competent for the registered office city
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founding members, personally or through attorneys-in-fact, appear before the notary to execute the Escritura de Constitución. The deed must include the name certificate, identity of members, subscription and payment of the share capital, bylaws, registered office, corporate object covering wholesale trading of crude oil and refined petroleum products, and the administrative organ (Administrador Único). The notary issues first and second copies and sends telematic notices to AEAT and the registry.
required_dossiers: Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social
Bank certificate of deposit or notarial capital statement
Project of bylaws reviewed by legal counsel
NIE or passport of all members and directors
Tax identification data of corporate shareholders
AML documentation and beneficial ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises formal defects, amend the deed or execute a ratification deed; if a notarial veto persists, request a second opinion from the Registradores association or restructure the defective clauses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Provisional tax identification number (NIF provisional) and census registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — local Delegación or CIRCE single window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within ten business days of deed execution, file model 036 requesting the provisional NIF, attaching a certified first copy of the deed and the director's identification. Declare the commencement of activity under IAE epígrafe 613 (wholesale of petroleum products). The provisional NIF is later confirmed as definitive after registry enrollment.
required_dossiers: First copy of the public deed
Form 036
NIE or passport of the director
Certificate of registered office address
Proof of payment of notarial and registry aranceles
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If model 036 is queried, correct inconsistent data (e.g., ISIC/IAE classification) and resubmit within the granted period; late-filing penalties may be reduced through voluntary regularisation before formal notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the provincial commercial registry and publication in BORME
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office; Registro Mercantil Central for BORME publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the first copy of the deed, the provisional NIF certificate and the stamped model 036 to the Registro Mercantil Provincial. The registrar qualifies the deed and, upon enrollment, the company acquires legal personality. The registry then publishes the incorporation in the Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil (BORME), and the blocked share capital is released to the company's free disposal.
required_dossiers: First copy of the public deed
Provisional NIF certificate
Model 036 stamped by AEAT
Proof of payment of registry arancel and stamp duty, if applicable
Certificate of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a calificación desfavorable, cure defects within 60 days by deed of subsanation; appeal an unfounded qualification to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation labor, social security and municipal operational filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS); municipal tax office (Ayuntamiento); regional Dirección General de Industria
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company with TGSS as employer (código de cuenta de cotización), file model 036/037 to confirm the definitive NIF, apply for the municipal Licencia de Apertura for the administrative office, and obtain the IAE settlement for the petroleum wholesale activity. Promotores must legalize the corporate books at the Registro Mercantil within the statutory deadline.
required_dossiers: TGSS registration forms TA.6/TA.7
Definitive NIF and census certificate
Municipal IAE declaration (model 840)
Fire-safety certification of the premises
Social security affiliation record of the director, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late registrations incur penalties; TGSS surcharges may be reduced by applying the reduced-surcharge mechanism and paying the base amount before formal warning; municipal licences may be regularized through a declaración responsable where zoning conditions are met.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (Secretaría de Estado de Energía) jointly with the Consejería de Industria of the autonomous community where the registered office or storage facility is located; Ministerio de Industria, Comercio y Turismo for industrial installation oversight.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorización administrativa previa como distribuidor al por mayor de productos petrolíferos under Article 42 of Ley 34/1998, de 7 de octubre, del Sector de Hidrocarburos, and mandatory inscription in the Registro de Distribuidores al por mayor de Productos Petrolíferos administered by CORES (Corporación de Reservas Estratégicas de Productos Petrolíferos); municipal Licencia de Actividad/Apertura for the trading office and, where physical storage is operated, the Autorización de Instalaciones Petrolíferas under Real Decreto 2085/1994 issued by the regional industrial authority.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico — Dirección General de Calidad y Evaluación Ambiental; autonomous community environmental department when the facility is below state thresholds
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Pure wholesale brokerage without storage or cargo handling is exempt from EIA but remains subject to urban zoning and atmospheric activity authorization; storage of petroleum products between 200 tonnes and 200,000 tonnes triggers Simplified EIA (Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental Simplificada) under Annex II, Group 5 of Ley 21/2013; storage above 200,000 tonnes requires Full EIA under Annex I, Group 5 of Ley 21/2013.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to public sewer must comply with Real Decreto 817/2015: total petroleum hydrocarbons less than 15 mg/L, COD less than 125 mg/L, TSS less than 35 mg/L, pH 6-9; marine bunker loading terminals must achieve a VOC recovery rate of at least 90% under Real Decreto 210/2013 and Directive 2010/75/EU BAT conclusions; oil residues and slops must be managed as hazardous waste under Ley 7/2022 and Real Decreto 679/2006, with registered waste producer status and transfer records.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety compliance certificate under the Reglamento de Seguridad contra Incendios en Establecimientos Industriales (Real Decreto 513/2017), supported by an authorized control body (OCA) periodic inspection; structural load clearance via the Inspección Técnica de la Edificación (ITE) of the commercial premises; occupational health and safety plan under Ley 31/1995 with risk evaluation under Real Decreto 39/1997; where petroleum products are stored, a self-protection plan (autoprotección) under Real Decreto 393/2007 coordinated with municipal fire services.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - Spanish Tax Agency, official portal https://www.agenciatributaria.gob.es/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Spanish SL entities obtain NIF automatically upon registration with the Registro Mercantil. Foreign entities must apply for NIF to AEAT with proof of tax residency and economic activity in Spain.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections; hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD Directive apply for certain cross-border structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory facturación electrónica; SII real-time reporting for VAT returns; digital invoice stamping (franquicia) required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT on exports of goods outside the EU; intra-EU supplies under reverse charge. Offshore services subject to place-of-supply rules.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fines up to 100% of evaded VAT plus interest; retrospective clawback of refunds with surcharges and potential criminal liability for fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain operates under a fully convertible euro currency regime within the Eurozone. Capital account transactions are unrestricted for EU entities. Current account transactions including trade settlements and service fees are freely convertible at market rates. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are permitted after corporate tax settlement and beneficial ownership verification under CRS/FATCA reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spanish law imposes no mandatory surrender of export proceeds to local banks. Foreign currency receipts must be repatriated within 10 working days. Banks require supporting documents such as commercial invoices and export permits. Settlement occurs at prevailing market rates with full disclosure.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility for offshore digital EMIs due to stringent AML regulations classifying energy commodity trading as high-risk. Spanish fintech platforms impose full KYC and may restrict or prohibit services for oil trading activities.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance of directors and authorized signatories is mandatory for initial KYC interviews at Spanish commercial banks for high-risk entities. Remote video KYC is permitted for subsequent verifications but not for first-time onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions screening hits on beneficial owners or trading partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficial ownership declaration, trade contracts, shipping documents, and independent legal opinions

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent transaction patterns with declared wholesale brokerage scope
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Purchase orders, export permits, bank references, and proof of legitimate fuel oil flows

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound routing uses Spanish IBAN accounts via SWIFT MT103 or SEPA with purpose codes 'CAPITAL_CONTRIBUTION' or 'EQUITY_INJECTION'. Verification requires shareholder agreements, incorporation certificates, and tax ID proofs.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements cleared via SWIFT MT103 for wire transfers or Commercial Letters of Credit for structured trade finance. Standby Letters of Credit are permissible for commodity trading.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT Return (Modelo 390) - annual summary of quarterly VAT settlements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 January following the taxable calendar year (fiscal year = 31 December)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Flat penalty EUR 200 for late filing; up to EUR 4,000 if inaccurate data is provided; possible proportional surcharges if VAT was due.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Third-Party Transaction Report (Modelo 347) - transactions exceeding EUR 3,005.06 per counterpart
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 20 February following the reporting calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty EUR 150 per data item omitted or false, capped at EUR 10,000 per taxpayer; failure to file may attract a minimum penalty of EUR 1,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporation Income Tax Return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Modelo 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 25 July after the tax period if the fiscal year ends on 31 December (within 6 months and 25 days of year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge 5% plus 1% per month on tax due (max 15%) with default interest from month 13; fixed penalty EUR 200 if no amount payable; penalties may reach 100% of tax due for non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Annual Accounts (Cuentas Anuales) - balance sheet, P&L, notes, audit report (if applicable), and approval certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Mercantile Registry of the Province (Registro Mercantil Provincial)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval at the ordinary AGM (must be held by 30 June for calendar year); for 31 December year-end, filing due by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Commercial registry closure (cierre registral) prohibiting any subsequent inscriptions until filing; fine from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000 imposed by the registrar; personal liability of directors for damages.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit when, for two consecutive years, the company meets any two of the following: total assets > EUR 2,850,000; annual net turnover > EUR 5,700,000; average workforce > 50 employees. Audits also mandatory for listed, credit, insurance, and other public-interest companies regardless of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General Contable) for individual statutory accounts under the Commercial Code; IFRS as adopted by the EU for consolidated accounts of listed groups (Regulation (EC) 1606/2002).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO confirmation is required in Spain. However, the company must maintain a UBO register and update the Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Registro de Titularidades Reales) within one month of any change in beneficial ownership or in the information originally filed.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Inventory and Annual Accounts Book (Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 450 - 1,500 per year for registered office / corporate compliance agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - 20,000 per year depending on volume of transactions and internal controls

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Newly formed entities generally apply a 15% rate in the first profitable tax period and the immediately following period, subject to statutory eligibility and anti-abuse conditions. Small entities may qualify for reduced rates under applicable annual legislation. Qualifying research and development, technological innovation, audiovisual production, employment, and investment incentives may reduce the effective tax burden. Tax holidays are not generally available to ordinary energy-commodity trading companies. Spanish tax losses are legally carried forward without a fixed expiry period, subject to annual utilization limitations, ownership-change restrictions, anti-abuse rules, and documentation requirements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Corporate Income Tax and Non-Resident Income Tax return for permanent establishments, filed electronically through the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) electronic headquarters using a qualified electronic certificate or approved representative authorization. Modelo 220 applies only to tax-consolidated groups.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within the 25 calendar days following the six months after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year company closing on 31 December, the ordinary filing period is 1 July through 25 July of the following year, subject to statutory weekend and public-holiday adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate name, Spanish tax identification number, registered address, tax period start and end dates, legal form, principal activity, and filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Spanish entity's NIF. A non-resident shareholder is not a substitute for the Spanish SL's own tax identification, registered-office, accounting, and filing data.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal form, tax group membership, size classification, related-party status, and applicable special regimes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose foreign parentage, participation in a multinational group, tax-consolidation status, and any applicable international or special-regime election.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss according to Spanish GAAP or accepted accounting standards, reconciled to the tax computation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign accounting records must be reconciled to Spanish statutory accounts and translated or supported where necessary. Commodity inventory, derivatives, freight, storage, demurrage, and financing entries require traceable documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary adjustments for depreciation, provisions, impairment, non-deductible expenses, exempt income, participation exemptions, interest limitation, and other tax rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Spanish deductibility rules to payments to foreign affiliates, including arm's-length pricing, beneficial-ownership analysis, withholding compliance, and anti-hybrid rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening losses, losses utilized during the period, current-period losses, and closing balances, subject to statutory utilization limits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain evidence of the losses and ownership history. Significant changes in direct or indirect ownership may restrict utilization where statutory anti-loss-trafficking conditions are met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base, applicable rate, gross corporate income tax, deductions, credits, and final liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not apply treaty reductions to the Spanish company's corporate income tax rate. Treaties generally allocate taxing rights between Spain and other states rather than replacing domestic corporate tax computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Payments made under Modelo 202 and, where applicable, withholding or installment credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile all Modelo 202 payments and Spanish withholding certificates. Excess payments may be offset or refunded through the annual return, subject to AEAT verification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Required disclosures concerning related-party transactions, transfer-pricing documentation, connected-party income and expenses, and group reporting obligations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report cross-border transactions with foreign parent, subsidiaries, treasury companies, traders, brokers, logistics entities, and financing vehicles consistently with transfer-pricing records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Spanish bank account or other permitted account information for refunds and payment arrangements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The account holder and refund documentation must be consistent with the Spanish taxpayer. Foreign-bank arrangements may require additional validation by AEAT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Submission using the taxpayer's electronic certificate or authorized representative, followed by preservation of the registration number and complete filed return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign directors and shareholders normally require a Spanish NIF and an authorized electronic representative or Spanish-certified filing provider.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without prior AEAT notice generally triggers a surcharge of 1% plus 1 percentage point for each complete month of delay, capped at 12 months; after 12 months, the surcharge is generally 15% plus late-payment interest. Filing after an AEAT notice may produce a tax penalty generally ranging from 50% to 150% of unpaid tax, subject to aggravating, conformity, and prompt-payment reductions. Failure to make Modelo 202 installments may generate interest and penalties. Deliberate tax fraud exceeding EUR 120,000 per tax period may constitute a criminal offense.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202, payment on account of Corporate Income Tax, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters. Modelo 222 applies to entities within a consolidated tax group.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally 1 to 20 April, October, and December; electronic filing and payment is generally available through the 15th calendar day for direct-debit arrangements, subject to the applicable annual calendar and tax-group rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIF, corporate name, tax period, tax year, and applicable payment-on-account regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Spanish SL's NIF and identify any consolidated-group or special-regime status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax-liability method or current-period tax-base method, where the statutory conditions for the latter apply.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select the method validly elected or mandated for the entity. Reconcile the calculation with Modelo 200 and management accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Relevant tax liability or current-period taxable base used to calculate the advance payment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude amounts that are not legally included in the selected method. Verify foreign withholding credits and other offsets separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory percentage applied to the installment base and resulting payment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the rate applicable to the entity and group status for the relevant tax year; do not substitute treaty withholding rates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Payment reference, bank debit, or other authorized settlement method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain bank evidence and reconcile the payment to the annual Modelo 200.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: The same late-filing surcharges generally apply where the taxpayer files voluntarily before notification. Failure after notice may lead to a penalty based on the unpaid installment, together with late-payment interest and collection proceedings.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish withholding generally applies to dividends and other profit distributions paid by a Spanish SL. Domestic exemptions may apply, including the EU Parent-Subsidiary regime where the recipient is a qualifying EU parent holding at least 10% for the required uninterrupted one-year period and anti-abuse conditions are satisfied. Treaty rates commonly reduce the rate to 5%, 10%, or 15%, depending on the treaty, ownership level, beneficial ownership, and applicable limitation provisions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a current certificate of tax residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority, verify beneficial ownership, ownership percentage and holding period, treaty eligibility, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose restrictions, and anti-abuse requirements. Provide the documentation to the Spanish payer and retain it with the payment records. Apply the reduced rate only where Spanish procedural requirements and the relevant treaty permit relief at source; otherwise withhold 19% and pursue the applicable refund procedure through AEAT. The Spanish payer must declare and pay withholding through Modelo 123 and provide annual recipient information through Modelo 193.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The domestic Spanish withholding rate is generally 19% for interest and royalties paid to non-residents, subject to exemptions and special rules. Interest and royalty payments to qualifying associated companies in EU Member States may be exempt under the EU Interest and Royalties regime where the minimum participation, holding-period, subject-to-tax, beneficial-owner, and anti-abuse requirements are met. Tax treaties may reduce or eliminate withholding, commonly providing maximum rates of approximately 5% to 15% for royalties and 0% to 15% for interest. Treaty relief requires residence, beneficial ownership, and anti-abuse evidence. Related-party financing and IP charges must also satisfy Spanish transfer-pricing and interest-deduction rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 250,000 in aggregate related-party transactions of the same type with the same related person during the tax period is the principal threshold commonly triggering the Spanish simplified documentation exemption boundary. Full Local File requirements may apply below this amount depending on transaction type, taxpayer status, group circumstances, and special rules. A Master File is generally required for Spanish entities belonging to a multinational or consolidated group unless a statutory exemption applies. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to qualifying multinational groups with consolidated annual revenue of at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not operate a standalone, generally applicable Economic Substance Regulation equivalent to the UAE ESR. Substance remains relevant under the General Anti-Avoidance Rule, conflict-in-application doctrine, beneficial-ownership requirements, principal-purpose analysis, controlled foreign company rules, anti-hybrid rules, interest limitation, EU anti-abuse provisions, and treaty interpretation. A Spanish SL trading marine fuel oil and distillates should maintain adequate Spanish decision-making, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises or demonstrable logistical infrastructure, risk control, banking controls, inventory and title documentation, customer and supplier management, and commercially justified functions. Artificial conduit entities, circular financing, commissionaire arrangements lacking functions, and unsupported low-tax profit allocation are high-risk.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing sales, fabricating fuel deliveries, manipulating bills of lading or quality certificates, using false invoices, understating customs or excise values, or claiming deductions without genuine transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative tax penalties can generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, plus interest and recovery costs. Deliberate tax fraud exceeding EUR 120,000 may constitute a criminal offense punishable generally by imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and a fine of 1 to 6 times the defrauded amount; aggravated cases, including amounts exceeding EUR 600,000 or organized conduct, may carry imprisonment of 2 to 6 years and higher fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may incur criminal liability, civil restitution, tax subsidiary liability, fines, and disqualification from public office or management. Asset preservation, precautionary measures, and judicial travel restrictions may be ordered in appropriate proceedings; travel bans and imprisonment are not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Value Added Tax carousel fraud and customs or excise evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Missing-trader transactions, fictitious intra-EU acquisitions, false export evidence, diversion of excise goods, misclassification of petroleum products, or claiming VAT refunds without genuine supply chains.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT assessments, repayment of refunds, interest, administrative penalties, customs debt, seizure, and potential criminal prosecution may arise. Criminal tax fraud thresholds and penalties may apply where the statutory elements and amount thresholds are met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable where they knowingly participate, consent, negligently supervise, or facilitate the conduct. Courts may order asset attachment, restitution, management disqualification, and imprisonment in criminal cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Allocating trading profits to foreign affiliates without corresponding functions, risks, assets, personnel, or decision-making; unsupported management fees, brokerage commissions, financing charges, guarantees, or IP royalties; or failing to maintain Local File and Master File documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may adjust taxable income to the arm's-length result, impose documentation and valuation penalties, deny deductions, apply withholding tax, and charge late-payment interest. Related-party transaction documentation penalties may apply per omitted, inaccurate, or incomplete data, subject to statutory caps and minimums.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face tax subsidiary liability where statutory negligence or intentional cooperation is established, particularly after unpaid assessments or improper distributions. Criminal liability normally requires fraudulent intent and satisfaction of criminal tax thresholds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, royalties, commissions, or service fees to non-residents without withholding, applying treaty relief without a valid residence certificate, or failing to report Modelo 123 or Modelo 193 information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Spanish payer may owe the omitted withholding, late-payment interest, and administrative penalties. Treaty relief may be denied where beneficial ownership, residence, anti-abuse, or procedural conditions are not satisfied.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur subsidiary tax liability and administrative sanctions where they caused or negligently permitted non-compliance. Personal criminal exposure requires intentional conduct satisfying the applicable criminal provisions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, beneficial ownership, and treaty abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a paper company as a conduit, routing dividends or interest through an entity lacking commercial substance, concealing the ultimate beneficial owner, or manufacturing ownership chains solely to obtain treaty or EU exemptions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Benefits may be denied under domestic anti-abuse rules, the applicable treaty, EU anti-abuse provisions, or beneficial-ownership doctrines. Additional tax, interest, penalties, withholding assessments, and criminal consequences may follow where fraud is proven.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may face tax liability, money-laundering exposure, asset restraint, management disqualification, and criminal sanctions. Piercing the corporate veil is fact-dependent and is not automatic merely because the company has foreign ownership.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained third-party payments, failing to identify customers or beneficial owners, ignoring sanctions or vessel red flags, processing opaque trade-finance structures, or failing to report suspicious activity to SEPBLAC where legally required.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Spain's AML framework, serious and very serious infringements may generate significant monetary penalties, including penalties calculated by reference to transaction value, profit, or annual turnover, together with public or private reprimands, temporary activity restrictions, and management disqualification. Criminal money-laundering liability may include imprisonment and fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and responsible managers may be personally sanctioned or prosecuted where they consented to, tolerated, or negligently failed to prevent the breach. Asset freezing and judicial travel restrictions may be imposed by competent authorities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Supplying petroleum products to sanctioned jurisdictions, vessels, companies, banks, or beneficial owners; circumventing EU sanctions through ship-to-ship transfers, falsified origin, transshipment, or alternative payment rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines, transaction nullification, asset freezes, license restrictions, customs measures, banking termination, and criminal prosecution may apply under EU and Spanish sanctions legislation. Penalties depend on the specific sanctions regime and conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may face personal administrative or criminal liability, asset seizure, management bans, and imprisonment where knowing or reckless participation is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining off-book accounts, falsifying inventory or title records, backdating contracts, manipulating commodity valuation, concealing related-party dealings, or destroying audit and trade documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax assessments, accounting penalties, regulatory sanctions, denial of deductions, and criminal offenses relating to false accounting, insolvency, or document fraud may apply. The company may also lose evidentiary credibility in AEAT, customs, banking, and criminal proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil damages, creditor claims, tax liability, disqualification, and criminal penalties, including imprisonment where statutory elements are met.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends while the company lacks distributable profits, concealing losses, stripping assets before tax payment, paying related parties ahead of creditors, or continuing operations while insolvent without required action.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Distributions may be recoverable, directors may be liable for company losses, and insolvency proceedings may classify the insolvency as culpable. Creditors, AEAT, and insolvency administrators may pursue restitution and clawback claims.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face joint or subsidiary civil liability, disqualification from administering third-party assets, personal contribution to the insolvency deficit in qualifying cases, and criminal liability for insolvency-related offenses.
